Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout artifacts—including both required wake views—before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll also follow the fish-control transfer skill and record any mechanism that actually informs the policy.

The workspace requires a pre-edit visual diagnosis, durable guidance, and a final policy-contract check; CFD is explicitly out of scope. I’m now applying the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to compare both 3D views, and the explicitly requested `fish-control-primitives` skill to extract only a transferable body-frame feedback invariant.

The visual comparison is clean: all sampled runs are self-propelled captures with alternating, spatially coherent wakes; the strongest run reaches the capture circle sooner, while the weaker prefill follows nearly the same route and wake topology but closes more slowly. There is no visible instability or wake-breakdown failure to “fix,” so I’m treating late closure—not carrier generation—as the remaining control problem and am cross-checking that against trajectory, load, and saturation columns now.

The completed evidence now isolates two compatible positive changes against the same v30 base: response-gated release is best (`18.7550 T`, integral `2.05886 L`), while bidirectional rejected-steering allocation also improves capture (`18.8705 T`, integral `2.06891 L`). Centering the actuator half-cycle detector is a reproducible negative. I’ll consult the shelf references before deciding whether the two positive mechanisms have a defensible invariant-level combination; no published gains or route details will transfer.

The shelf supports a small, testable combination: keep the traveling-wave carrier local to each joint, recover only target-derived residual lost at the other joint’s bound, and release withheld cadence only after body-frame closure confirms useful motion. This matches the two independent completed improvements and explicitly excludes the failed derivative common-mode idea. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification boundary before touching the solver, as required by the visual-evidence skill.

The solver now contains exactly one merged policy candidate: the best completed closing-response controller plus reverse recovery of only posterior-rejected target steering. Its oscillator, route projection, redirect, and hard limits remain intact. I’m updating the durable experience bank with the reusable result boundaries—especially that raw half-cycle phase beats centered phase here, and posterior joint-rate “correction” must not be revived.

The merged policy passes a deterministic 26,244-state smoke sweep: every command is finite and remains inside the declared acceleration envelope. I’m now invoking the workspace’s required check runner for the parent-guidance materiality check, parameter-schema guard, and no-CFD policy audit.

The named check-runner profile could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account. I’ve read the profile and will execute its three prescribed checks directly and separately, preserving the same validation contract and still avoiding CFD.

The guidance check found a workspace-rendering defect before comparing content: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so the checker sees two parents and exits. I’m inspecting the checker and the duplicate lines; if they are exact duplicates, I’ll remove only the redundant marker so the mandated semantic comparison can run.

The first two prescribed checks now pass. The only repair was removing an exact duplicate assigned-parent marker from the rendered root README so the guidance checker could identify its single baseline. The policy-contract invocation also passes; I’m running the final editable-boundary check next.

All required checks pass: guidance materiality, lightweight policy contract, editable boundary, the 26,244-state finite/bounded sweep, and an explicit schema audit confirming all 59 `params.FIELD` references are declared. No CFD was run; the new combination remains a falsifiable candidate for downstream evaluation.

Completed exactly one Phase 2 candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) combines positive-closing cadence release with bounded bidirectional rejected-steering recovery.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, inherited failure boundaries, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:107) now contains the evidence-backed reusable lesson.

Validation passed:

- Guidance materiality check
- Lightweight policy contract
- Editable-boundary check
- All 59 parameter references declared
- 26,244 finite, actuator-bounded test states

No CFD was run. I also removed one exact duplicate parent marker from `README.md` that prevented the mandated guidance checker from identifying its baseline.
